statements.t: These statements include, but are not limited to, statements related to our expectations regarding the performance of our business, profitability, liquidity and capital; anticipated benefits of our securities repositioning and other strategic balance sheet actions including, among others, a strengthened credit risk profile, increased capital efficiency, and an enhanced earnings profile; and other non-historical…

During the second quarter of 2026, the Company executed several strategic balance sheet actions, including (i) the repositioning of $2.3 billion of lower-yielding HTM securities, (ii) the transfer of $827.0 million of selected commercial real estate and multi-family construction loans from HFI to HFS as part of a targeted loan sale process, and (iii) the redemption of $385.0 million of subordinated debt.
In connection with the targeted loan sale process, the Company transferred $827.0 million of loans to HFS during the second quarter of 2026.
The majority of the targeted loan sales closed during the third quarter of 2026, and the Company completed the remaining targeted loan sales on October 21, 2026.

The second quarter provision was elevated by the strategic balance sheet repositioning activities related to the targeted loan sale process, the impact of loan growth and higher loss given default rates on CRE and multi-family construction loans, offset partially by improved risk ratings in our HFI portfolio.

The provision for the 2026 period included a provision for loan losses of $180.2 million, reflecting the impact of the targeted loan sale process and the impact of loan growth, offset partially by improved risk ratings for our HFI portfolio.

Due to the significant impact of these actions on projected annual earnings, in the second quarter, the Company began calculating its tax provision using a year-to-date effective tax rate approach rather than the estimated annual effective tax rate method.

The Company's September 30, 2026 balance sheet reflects the effects of several strategic balance sheet actions that occurred in the second quarter of 2026, including the repositioning of $2.3 billion of lower-yielding HTM securities, the transfer of $827.0 million of loans from HFI to HFS as part of the targeted loan sale process, and the retirement of $385.0 million of subordinated debt.
As part of our management of the loans held in our portfolio, on occasion we will transfer loans from HFI to HFS.

The increase was primarily driven by the transfer of $827.0 million of CRE and multi-family construction loans from HFI to HFS in the second quarter of 2026 as part of the Company's targeted loan sale process, offset partially by $615.2 million of loan sales during the nine months ended September 30, 2026, including a majority of the targeted loan sales that closed during the period.

In estimating the ACL, we consider multiple forward‑looking economic scenarios, with scenario selection and weighting reflecting current economic conditions and downside risk over the reasonable and supportable forecast period.
We believe the ACL appropriately reflects expected credit losses inherent in the portfolio as of the reporting date.

Special mention and classified loans and leases were impacted by the transfer of $827.0 million of loans from HFI to HFS in the second quarter of 2026 as part of the Company's targeted loan sale process.

Classified loans and leases decreased by $293.0 million to $507.4 million at September 30, 2026 compared to $800.3 million at December 31, 2025, primarily reflecting the transfer of certain loans to HFS in the second quarter of 2026 as part of the Company's targeted loan sale process.
Our obligations also include off-balance sheet arrangements consisting of loan commitments, of which only a portion is expected to be funded, and standby letters of credit.
